It solves the problem of reconstruction artifacts and inversion ambiguities inherent in traditional NLOS imaging by automatically self-calibrating imaging parameters during the reconstruction process, eliminating the need for manual selection of filtering functions and parameters [S1].

The claim states that the method solves reconstruction artifacts and inversion ambiguities inherent in traditional NLOS imaging by automatically self-calibrating imaging parameters during reconstruction, thereby eliminating the need for manual selection of filtering functions and parameters. Source [S1] explicitly supports this in the abstract/introduction section: 'These methods are prone to reconstruction artifacts due to inversion ambiguities and capture noise, which are typically mitigated through the manual selection of filtering functions and parameters. We introduce a fully-differentiable end-to-end NLOS inverse rendering pipeline that self-calibrates the imaging parameters during the reconstruction of hidden scenes...'. It further confirms in the notes and text that unlike existing methods relying on manual selection, this method self-calibrates parameters automatically via gradient descent.
